content: Never commit Python cache files (__pycache__) or transient database/test artifacts (test.db-journal, *.db, *.sqlite-journal) to version control — add these patterns to .gitignore and remove any that were already committed
Never use CORS allow_origins=['*'] in production code — make CORS configuration environment-dependent with specific origins
Make hardcoded business values (ticket prices, cache TTL, rates) and database connection URLs configurable via constants or environment variables instead of embedding them in code
Test public interface methods rather than private methods directly (e.g. avoid testing _validate_venue_data() itself; test the public methods that use it)
Remove unused imports to maintain clean code

Never open, submit, or defer-to-CI a PR with known failing, incomplete, or unverified tests — including descriptions admitting tests 'could not be run/verified in the workspace' or 'some tests failing — needs review'. Repeated failure mode (PRs #191, #192). Resolve environment/test issues and confirm tests pass locally before opening the PR; such disclaimers should block merge regardless of other checks — don't defer to reviewers or CI.
Use request body with proper schema instead of query parameters for POST endpoints

Validate data integrity constraints at the model level (e.g. prevent negative durations, ensure end_date > start_date) and add business rule validation beyond basic schema validation (duplicate venues, capacity limits, etc.)
Implement comprehensive test coverage for all CRUD operations — include dedicated test classes for POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints
Use in-memory or shared test databases with proper cleanup instead of separate test database files — separate db files cause test isolation issues
Implement proper format validation for structured data fields — e.g. zip_code regex '^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$' and HttpUrl type for website fields
Whitelist allowed fields for update operations — don't rely on hasattr() checks without validating against dangerous fields like 'id'

Keep PRs strictly scoped to their stated purpose — never bundle unrelated housekeeping changes (e.g. .gitignore edits, config tweaks) into a feature/test PR, even if reasonable on its own; split such changes into a separate PR. Recurring issue (e.g. PR #307 bundled .gitignore into a claimed test PR) — review should explicitly verify the diff matches the PR's stated scope before approving.
Always verify all imported modules and dependencies exist before referencing them — missing files like database.py, models.py, schemas.py cause critical import errors and application failures
Always ensure database migration enum values match model definitions exactly — mismatches like migration 'PLANNING' vs model 'planning' cause runtime failures
Use proper foreign key relationships in tests instead of hardcoded IDs (e.g. venue_id=1) — hardcoded values don't test real relationships and fail under real database constraints
Always implement CSRF protection and XSS escaping when using HTMX forms — use Flask-WTF CSRF tokens on data-modifying endpoints (hx-post, hx-delete) and escape user content with {{ content|e }}

Mock chained method calls require explicit return_value assignment at each level — use mock_db.query.return_value.filter.return_value.first.return_value instead of mock_db.query().filter().first.return_value
Never manually manage database sessions by calling next(get_db()) and db.close() — use FastAPI dependency injection or proper session context management
Never mix framework-specific syntax between different frameworks — e.g. using Flask url_for() in FastAPI templates causes incompatibility errors
Use proper SQLAlchemy 2.0 session patterns in tests with contextlib.contextmanager — avoid manual session management with try/except StopIteration handling
Always call database initialization functions or document their usage — e.g. a defined but never-called create_tables() leaves tables uncreated

Quality gate 'coverage' has persistently failed at 0% (threshold 70) from 2026-04-16 through 2026-09-14, and intermittently reports 'not_run' instead of 'fail' (as of 2026-09-24) — indicates coverage instrumentation (e.g. pytest-cov) isn't properly wired into the test run/report step; fix the tooling config, not just add more tests

Quality gate 'e2e_tests' has repeatedly reported passed=0 AND failed=0 with status=fail (total varies 11-27, e.g. total=24 on 2026-09-25) from 2026-04-16 through 2026-09-25, indicating a persistent test collection/execution error (import failure, missing fixture, app not starting) rather than genuine assertion failures. A brief 'pass' status was observed at 2026-09-24 18:30 but the failure recurred later the same day and again on 2026-09-25 — treat as unresolved and unstable; needs root-cause fix, not just re-running

Quality gate 'security' reports status 'not_run' (as opposed to pass/fail) — indicates the security scan step itself isn't being invoked in the cycle pipeline, a wiring/instrumentation gap rather than an actual code quality issue

Confirmed: the merge pipeline does not treat coverage, security, or e2e_tests as blocking quality gates, and review-flagged critical issues (e.g. PR claims to add tests but includes no test code, or bundles unrelated changes) also do not block merging — only unit_tests status appears to gate merge decisions. One cycle produced 3 PRs opened but 0 merged despite unit/e2e tests passing, likely due to an untested-code issue (see PR #307). Verify and fix CI/review wiring so these gates actually block merges

Registering a SQLAlchemy event listener (e.g. a query counter like `_count_queries`) on the shared test `engine` imported from tests.conftest causes it to persist globally across all connections and tests rather than scoping to the single test under measurement — attach listeners to a per-test connection/session instead, and remove them deterministically (context manager or fixture teardown), not a bare finally block

PR titles/descriptions claiming to 'write tests' or 'close #issue' must be cross-checked against actual diff content before merge — PR #307 claimed to add city-filtering tests and close #306 but contained zero test file changes, indicating the merge pipeline isn't validating claim-vs-diff consistency.
Never remove essential dependencies that are still in use — pytest, pydantic, alembic, aiosqlite, httpx are needed for testing, schemas, database operations, and FastAPI TestClient imports
Use modern SQLAlchemy 2.0 syntax — DeclarativeBase instead of declarative_base(), .where() instead of .filter() on count() results
Use FastAPI lifespan context manager instead of deprecated @app.on_event('startup') for FastAPI 0.104.1+
Use SQLAlchemy's Enum type for proper database constraints instead of String — storing enum values as strings without db-level enum constraints reduces data integrity
Use Pydantic v2 syntax with `from_attributes = True` and `.model_dump()` instead of deprecated `orm_mode = True` and `.dict()`
Never enable SQL logging in production code — echo=True in the SQLAlchemy engine logs all SQL statements to console and should be configurable via environment variables

Never change frameworks without implementing the complete backend infrastructure — e.g. switching from FastAPI to Flask requires implementing all routes, models, and app setup before templates can function
Always implement pagination (limit/offset) on collection GET endpoints — missing pagination causes performance issues with large datasets
Implement foundational layers before dependent components — create models, services, and backend endpoints before writing tests or frontend code that depends on them
Avoid circular imports by placing shared Base classes in a separate module like models/base.py rather than defining them locally

Never open, submit, or claim a PR implements functionality, closes an issue, or adds tests when the diff doesn't actually contain those changes — verify diff contents match the PR title/description before opening/submitting. Repeated failure mode: PR #192 (entire changeset was a binary test.db-journal artifact), PR #257 (100% test additions with no schema/model/endpoint changes), PR #307 (claimed to add city-filtering backend tests and close an issue but diff only added a .gitignore entry). Such mismatched PRs should be rejected/closed, not merged.

Scope database/test-infrastructure changes narrowly. Switching SQLALCHEMY_TEST_DATABASE_URL from a file-based sqlite DB to 'sqlite://' in-memory with StaticPool is a global change affecting every test in the suite and needs explicit review of test isolation/ordering — don't apply such changes globally when only new fixtures need them
Always include referenced template files in PRs when implementing routes — referencing templates without including them breaks the application
API endpoints should return JSON data following REST conventions — returning raw HTML from API endpoints violates standards and complicates testing/maintenance
Integrate validation methods into models via SQLAlchemy's @validates decorator, or remove them — unconnected validation methods are dead code
Implement proper error handling for external dependencies — service methods should handle database connection failures and query timeouts gracefully with appropriate fallback responses
Implement comprehensive test coverage including dedicated unit tests for service layer business logic — endpoint tests alone are insufficient

PR #307 claimed to add backend tests for city filtering (issue #306) but contained zero test files in the diff — reinforces need to verify actual file changes match PR description before merge, not just the title/issue reference.

Do not bundle unrelated housekeeping changes (e.g. .gitignore entries like *.sqlite-journal) into PRs with a different stated purpose (e.g. adding tests) — keep PRs scoped to one concern per repo convention.

A PR claimed to add backend tests for city filtering (#306) but contained no test file, only an unrelated .gitignore change — always verify the actual diff contains the claimed implementation before opening/describing a PR as adding tests or closing an issue.

Unrelated housekeeping changes (e.g. .gitignore edits like adding *.sqlite-journal) were bundled into a PR whose stated purpose was writing tests — keep PRs scoped to their stated purpose and split unrelated changes into separate PRs.
